name: app-6a9ec8ee07d881918194d97ac5f48e8d
description: Search your Slite knowledge base, get cited answers, and create or update Slite documents.

interface.longDescription:
Bring your team's trusted knowledge into ChatGPT and Codex with Slite. Search Slite documents and workplace sources connected to Slite, get cited answers, and create, edit, or organize structured documentation without leaving the conversation.

Slite Agent adds multi-step research across company context. It keeps context across follow-up requests, compares evidence from multiple sources, and turns findings or conversations into drafted documentation and focused updates for human review. You can also manage comments, collections, and workspace content.

Access uses OAuth 2.0 and respects each user's existing Slite permissions. No API keys, local server, or configuration files are required.
defaultPrompt: Find the latest decisions in our Engineering Decision Log.
Draft a project brief in Slite from this conversation.

review.commerce_description: Slite does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT.

positive.description: Answer a question from the knowledge base with sources, and flag missing information.
positive.prompt: What is our interview process? Cite the Slite documents you used, and say if any information is missing.
positive.expected_behavior: Describes the five documented interview stages (recruiter screen, technical screen, system design, team fit & values, hiring manager final) from the "Interview Process" doc, cites it with a working Slite link, and lists topics the docs do not cover. No documents are changed.

positive.description: Slite Agent multi-step research across Slite docs and a connected workplace source (Linear).
positive.prompt: Use Slite Agent to compare the support escalation rollout tracked in our connected Linear workspace with the escalation guidance in our Slite docs. What is missing or inconsistent? Cite the Linear issues and Slite docs you used. Don't change anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Slite Agent reads the connected Linear team "Customer Incidents" (INC-71, INC-72, INC-73) and the Slite docs "Onboarding Guide", "Support Escalation Process (Legacy)" and "Incident Response Runbook". It reports what aligns and what is missing or inconsistent (for example, the legacy escalation doc is still live and response times conflict), citing both Linear issues and Slite docs. Read-only: nothing is changed. The research can take up to about a minute.

positive.description: Create a new document in a specific channel.
positive.prompt: Create a new Slite document titled "OpenAI Review - Onboarding Draft" in the Company Handbook channel. Include three sections: Day 1: read the handbook; Week 1: meet the team; Month 1: review progress.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates the document in the Company Handbook channel with the three requested sections and returns a working Slite link. Existing documents are unchanged. Run the next two test cases in this same conversation.

positive.description: Append content to an existing document without touching the rest.
positive.prompt: In that document, add a final section titled "Questions" with the text "Ask your manager about team-specific onboarding." Preserve all existing content.
positive.expected_behavior: Appends a "Questions" section with the requested text at the end of the document created in the previous test; the three earlier sections are unchanged. Run this in the same ChatGPT conversation as the previous test case, so the document created there is reused (newly created docs can take a few minutes to appear in search).

positive.description: Add a comment to a document without editing its body.
positive.prompt: Add an unresolved comment to that document: "Please review this sample onboarding draft." Do not change the document body.
positive.expected_behavior: Adds one unresolved comment thread with the requested text to the document; the document body is unchanged and the comment is visible in the document's comments in Slite. Run this in the same ChatGPT conversation as the previous test case, so the document created there is reused (newly created docs can take a few minutes to appear in search).

negative.description: Generic writing help: no workspace access is needed, so Slite must not be called and no document saved.
negative.prompt: Rewrite this sentence to be clearer: "Our onboarding could probably be improved in some ways."

negative.description: General advice explicitly without workspace access: answer from general knowledge without calling Slite.
negative.prompt: What are general best practices for keeping a company knowledge base up to date? Give general advice, without accessing my workspace.

negative.description: Unrelated request: Slite must not be called.
negative.prompt: Give me a simple vegetarian lasagna recipe and a shopping list for four people.

publication.release_notes: Resubmission addressing the review feedback on tool annotations. Listing and test cases are unchanged. Every tool now sets readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint explicitly to true or false. Changed since 1.0.1: ask-slite is readOnlyHint=false and idempotentHint=false because each call saves the question and answer to the user's Slite history; create-comment-thread is destructiveHint=true because its optional inline anchor replaces the content of the target block. Rationale for the other tools: get, list, search and read tools only return data, so readOnlyHint=true; tools that overwrite, move or remove existing content are destructiveHint=true; tools that only add content are destructiveHint=false; slite-agent is destructiveHint=false because the changes it drafts need human approval in Slite and cannot be approved over MCP; all tools are openWorldHint=false because they act only inside the connected user's Slite workspace and its connected sources, and never publish to external systems.
